questionText: A $32$-bit wide main memory unit with a capacity of $1\text{ GB}$ is built using $256\text{M} \times 4$-bit DRAM chips. The number of rows of memory cells in the DRAM chip is $2^{14}$. The time taken to perform one refresh operation is $50\text{ nanoseconds}$. The refresh period is $2\text{ milliseconds}$. The percentage (rounded to the closest integer) of the time available for performing the memory read/write operations in the main memory unit is _________.
explanation:
Step-by-step Solution:

1. Identify given parameter values:
- Number of rows in DRAM chip = $2^{14} = 16384$ rows.
- Time to refresh one row = $50\text{ ns} = 50 \times 10^{-9}\text{ seconds}$.
- Refresh period = $2\text{ ms} = 2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ seconds}$.

2. Calculate total refresh time per refresh period:
$\text{Total Refresh Time} = 16384 \times 50\text{ ns} = 819,200\text{ ns} = 0.8192\text{ ms}$.

3. Calculate percentage of time spent in refresh:
$\text{Refresh Overhead} = \left( \frac{0.8192\text{ ms}}{2\text{ ms}} \right) \times 100\% = 40.96\%$.

4. Calculate percentage of time available for Read/Write:
$\text{Available Time} = 100\% - 40.96\% = 59.04\%$.

Rounding $59.04\%$ to the closest integer yields $59$.
